definitions.explanation: The quality of being humble and yielding to others, particularly by lowering oneself. Central to the Japanese politeness system, especially in the context of humble language (謙譲語).

examples.japanese: {謙譲|けんじょう}の{美徳|びとく}を{大切|たいせつ}にする。
examples.english: To value the virtue of humility.

examples.japanese: {謙譲|けんじょう}の{気持|きも}ちを{忘|わす}れないようにしたい。
examples.english: I want to always keep a spirit of humility.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}を{学|まな}ぶとき、{謙譲語|けんじょうご}は{尊敬語|そんけいご}と{並|なら}んで{重要|じゅうよう}な{敬語|けいご}の{一種|いっしゅ}だ。
examples.english: When studying Japanese, humble language is an important type of keigo alongside honorific language.

notes:
USAGE:
{謙譲|けんじょう} is most commonly encountered in the compound {謙譲語|けんじょうご} (humble language), one of the three main categories of Japanese keigo ({敬語|けいご}). On its own, it describes the attitude of humble self-restraint.

COMPOUNDS:
- {謙譲語|けんじょうご} (humble language — lowers the speaker to show respect)
- {謙譲|けんじょう}の{美徳|びとく} (the virtue of humility)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {謙譲|けんじょう}な{態度|たいど} (a humble attitude)
- {謙譲|けんじょう}の{精神|せいしん} (a spirit of humility)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{謙虚|けんきょ} (humble, modest) is a more common everyday word for humility as a personal quality. {謙譲|けんじょう} has a more formal, traditional tone and is strongly associated with the keigo system.
